    • testOutOfOrderArchivedWALDoesNotSkipOlderWAL

      @Test public void testOutOfOrderArchivedWALDoesNotSkipOlderWAL() throws Exception
      WALs can be archived out of order, so a region server that took part in the log roll can have an archived WAL newer than its roll result while an older WAL is still in the WALs directory. The newer archived WAL must be deferred to a later backup instead of being backed up twice, and the older WAL must still end up in a backup.
      Throws:
      Exception

    • testWALOfDeadServerStillSplittingIsBackedUpAfterArchiving

      @Test public void testWALOfDeadServerStillSplittingIsBackedUpAfterArchiving() throws Exception
      A dead region server's WALs stay in its -splitting directory until WAL splitting finishes. An incremental backup that runs during the split must not lose them once they are archived.
      Throws:
      Exception

    • testOlderWALsOfDeadServerAreNotSkippedWhenNewerWALIsArchivedFirst

      @Test public void testOlderWALsOfDeadServerAreNotSkippedWhenNewerWALIsArchivedFirst() throws Exception
      WAL splitting archives a dead region server's WALs in parallel, so a newer WAL can be archived while older ones are still in the -splitting directory. Backing up the newer WAL must not move the boundary past the older ones.
      Throws:
      Exception

    • testDeadServerKeepsBoundaryWhileOldWALIsStillSplitting

      @Test public void testDeadServerKeepsBoundaryWhileOldWALIsStillSplitting() throws Exception
      A dead region server can keep an old WAL, already covered by its boundary, in its -splitting directory across several incremental backups. Its boundary must survive those backups, or a later backup would include that WAL again and could bring back deleted data.
      Throws:
      Exception
